name: App icon badge count
plain: Shows an unread number on the app icon.
meaning: A constant nudge to re-open the app. iOS needs alert-style permission for badges; Android launchers derive badges from active notifications, not from a number the app can set.

android.prompt_ui: Launcher dot or count from notifications

ios.prompt_ui: Badges toggle in the permission prompt
ios.store_policy: App Review 4.5.4: no numbers for ads

limits.headline: Can show a number on the app icon, if you allow badges
limits.user_action: You allow notifications and the Badges switch when the app asks
can: Show a count of unread items on the icon
Clear or change the count when you open the app
Show a dot or count on the Android icon, depending on your launcher
cannot: Show a badge on iPhone if you turned Badges off
Show exactly the same way on every Android launcher; Samsung and Xiaomi differ
Tell the app anything about you; it only shows a number
limits.reach_label: A single number on the icon
limits.differs: iPhone has a Badges toggle in the permission prompt. Android shows a dot or count that depends on the launcher.

story.what_it_is: The little red number on an app icon that shows unread items.

marketing.name: Badges
marketing.pitch: Apple lets apps show a number on the icon to tell you something new is waiting, if you allow it.

story.for_you: You see a number or dot on the icon and feel the urge to clear it. It tells you something is waiting without a sound.
story.for_makers: Makers know a red badge is one of the strongest nudges to reopen an app. It lifts daily use, so some apps are accused of making badges that never go away.

use_cases.example: Your chat app shows 12 on the icon so you see how many messages you missed.
A social app shows a count of likes and follows to pull you back.
An email app shows unread messages so you can triage from the home screen.
A shopping app shows a dot when a wishlist item goes on sale.
A game shows a badge when a free daily gift is ready to collect.
A growth team tests badge counts to see what brings back lapsed users.
A bank app shows a dot for a new statement or security notice.

risks: Can pressure you to keep checking
story.android_note: Android launchers show a dot or count taken from active notifications, not a number the app sets.
story.ios_note: iOS needs you to allow badges in the permission prompt.

technical_bounds: Cannot be set directly on stock Android
